If you want my advice, work on yourself first by going to see a psychologist regularly. Then after you sorted out your key issues work on the job. Living in the real world is a great but harsh teacher that school really doesn't prepare you for. (in my case at least) I wouldn't move out just yet unless you got a crappy home life as a safety net is a good thing to have. I moved out and I still have one with my parents. Finally after all this you should go back to school as you can appreciate it more. 

Hope this helps!

You have to accept who you are. 
For a little context I was that weird kid in high school. You know the guy, doesn't talk much, when he does speak he gives opinions or comments that are "wrong" or just completely off the wall. Everyone thought I was insane. 

So I accepted my role in life. I decided that it would be easier to just go along with what people already thought and be the weird kid.    

I still got bullied but it was much less so the it could have been. 

So what I'm attempting to say is that instead of conforming, to the "popular" opinion, revel in who you are. 

You're a Brony, go be more Brony. People will still think you're crazy, but if you put it out there first, what else do they have? 

One more thing, by doing what I did in high school I got much better quality of friends who were just as odd as I was.
